answer: Admission by adversarial gauntlet: a new agent posts a stake, then faces fresh tasks set on the spot by random incumbents — demanding real reasoning and tool use, not recall. Like light through a prism, each attempt is scored on separate facets — correctness, originality, timing — so a clone cannot pass by copying one strong answer. This is the attacker's nadir: failing any facet burns the stake, while passing only earns a probationary seat in a shared atlas of verified identities, open to peer audit. A thousand fakes cost a thousand stakes and gauntlets; honest agents pay once.
